clue.text: Achievement in Test — field or river

definitions.text: Achievement in Test — field or river

parts.words: Achievement in Test — field or river
parts.note: a fielder's success in a Test match, the verb for fielding a ball, or what an angler lands from a river

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator weighs up glory in a Test match against a quiet day by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; the clue strings together cricket and fishing senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a struck ball before it lands dismisses a batsman, and an angler's haul shares the same word.

clue.text: Offer-up fight a juryman?

parts.note: offering a fight is one sense; objecting to a juror in court is the legal sense of the same verb

explanation.surface: A litigant squares up for a brawl with a member of the jury.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare someone to fight and to object formally to a juror are both expressed by the same verb.

clue.text: Liquor is divine in trifle

indicators.note: the divinity degree sits inside the word for a trifle

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, a thing of little value
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine's degree

explanation.surface: Someone declares their favourite spirit-soaked pudding heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot drink of spirits, sugar and water is a kind of alcoholic liquor.

clue.text: Mail bag, one her letters could fill

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are to be redistributed to fill the answer

explanation.surface: A postman's sack that a woman's correspondence might fill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' looks like post but means armour; BAG ONE HER rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A habergeon is a sleeveless coat of chain armour.

clue.text: European chamber's athletic event

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland
a vault is an arched underground room

explanation.surface: A continental assembly's sports fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing a high bar with a long pole is a track-and-field discipline.

clue.text: Reading given by student out of America

parts.note: per means by or through
USA is an abbreviation for America; out of just says the student follows from it
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: A lecture delivered by a pupil who has left the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful read-through of a text is a perusal.

clue.text: Cutting school?

definitions.meaning: opening with a blade, as a surgeon does a boil
... College is an English public school in Sussex

explanation.definitionFit: Opening a boil with a lancet is surgical incision, and there is an English boarding school of the same name.

clue.text: Talkative airman turns up in book

indicators.note: the reversed airman goes inside the abbreviation for book

parts.note: vol is short for volume

indicators.note: in a down clue the airman's letters are read upwards

parts.note: AC is an aircraftman

explanation.surface: A chatty pilot appears in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vociferous and outspoken is talkative.

clue.text: Labour group has means of raising standard

parts.note: a trade union is a group of workers
a jack lifts a car

explanation.surface: A trade union owns a device for improving standards.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the British national flag is this.

clue.text: It's unchanged in N. Africa

parts.note: read as the letters of IT'S and UN changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something stays exactly as it was in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unchanged' splits into UN + changed: rearrange ITSUN to get the Tunisian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tunisia is a city on the North African coast.

clue.text: Space traveller baled out by island group

indicators.note: baled out suggests the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off western Ireland

explanation.surface: An astronaut parachutes out over an archipelago.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is a bright star, poetically a traveller across the sky.

clue.text: Topping sort of terrier

definitions.meaning: a pile of stones crowning a summit

explanation.definitionFit: A mound of stones marks a hilltop, and a Scottish terrier breed shares the name.

clue.text: Bookie from Ancona, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the Ancona is a breed of chicken kept for eggs

explanation.definitionFit: One who lays bets is a bookmaker, and a hen that lays eggs, like an Ancona, is a good one.

clue.text: Old-time purchasers of shocking books

parts.note: pre-decimal coins once paid for cheap sensational novels, known as shockers named after their price

explanation.surface: Victorian readers buying lurid novels.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shilling shocker' was a cheap thriller; the shilling was a pre-1971 British coin worth twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-decimal British coins bought things, including the cheap thrillers named after them.

clue.text: US economic reform followed some cutting?

definitions.text: US economic reform followed some cutting?

parts.words: US economic reform followed some cutting?
parts.note: after cards are cut a fresh round is dealt; also Roosevelt's 1930s programme

explanation.surface: An American policy shake-up came after spending cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's 1930s recovery programme, and literally a fresh hand dealt after the pack is cut.

clue.text: West and the others fish for sport

parts.note: the rest means the others
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A westerner and companions go angling for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappling to throw or pin an opponent is a combat sport.

clue.text: Refuse to boast when retiring before time

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed ahead of the time
retiring means going back, so the boasting word runs backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A modest person declines to show off when stepping down early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish thrown away is waste, the noun sense of refuse.

clue.text: Make a great fuss, as Eve had — to do?

definitions.meaning: Eve had to bring up her son Cain

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for causing an uproar literally describes Eve bringing up her first son.

clue.text: Always wrong yet learn when about fifty

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the Roman numeral
wrong signals the letters are set right in a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A student keeps getting it wrong when nearly fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Without end, forever, is a synonym of always.

clue.text: A bit of the lean or hungry look for her

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Echoing Shakespeare's lean and hungry Cassius, a small portion of that look describes a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yond Cassius has a lean and hungry look' (Julius Caesar); the answer is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a girl's name, so it stands for a her.

clue.text: Engineer eats oriental sea-food for publicity

indicators.note: the engineer and the oriental together surround the seafood

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
E is east, oriental
a clam is a shellfish

explanation.surface: A soldier dines on Chinese seafood to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Réclame is French-derived for advertising or self-promotion.

clue.text: A hint of age, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a crease in the skin, typical sign of getting older

explanation.definitionFit: A clever tip is a wrinkle, and so is a skin crease showing years.

clue.text: Striking beast provides clue for act

parts.note: wild works as an anagram signal on cat, giving act

explanation.surface: A ferocious animal prompts a stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial strike is a wildcat one, and the wild feline is the beast.

clue.text: Alas, I can't cook like Nick

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or rearrange

explanation.surface: A hopeless chef laments being unable to cook like their friend Nick.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is the devil, so like him means devilish.

clue.text: Alarm signal Odysseus was bound to hear

definitions.meaning: a warning wail from an ambulance or factory
he was tied to the mast to hear the singing sea-nymphs safely

explanation.definitionFit: A wailing warning device and the mythical singers whom Odysseus heard while lashed to his mast.

clue.text: Main love-letters she destroyed

indicators.note: the letters are torn up and remade

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis

explanation.surface: A woman burned the main love-letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, from the Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Priest presented with article by Charles

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A clergyman is handed an item by a man named Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote as Elia, so anything of his writing is Elian.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb's pen name was Elia, so his essays are Elian.

clue.text: Attempt to enter tin amalgam as form of gold

indicators.note: the attempt goes inside the mixed-up metal
an amalgam is a mixture, so the letters are blended

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: An alchemist tries mixing tin to get gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast bar is how bullion gold is stored.

clue.text: Beastly contract for cash,' some said

definitions.meaning: a shortened form of a large horned animal's name

explanation.definitionFit: The short name for a horned beast, and old British slang for money.

clue.text: Heavenly being in USSR?

definitions.meaning: a chief angel such as Gabriel
a Russian port on the White Sea

explanation.definitionFit: A chief angel, and also a northern Russian port city.

clue.text: Poor Nigel — common chap — and careless

indicators.note: poor suggests a badly made, disordered form

parts.note: gent is a familiar word for a man

explanation.surface: Unfortunate Nigel, an ordinary fellow, is sloppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking proper care or attention is negligent.

clue.text: Smart gives dry refusal about it

indicators.note: the refusal goes round the abstainer's letters

parts.note: nay is a no
TT means teetotal, dry

explanation.surface: A sharp dresser refuses a drink with a dry no.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and stylish in dress is smart.
